newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Belfox sees pan-European stock derivatives.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Belfox sees pan-European stock derivatives.

text.p: The Brussels futures and options exchange Belfox said on Monday that it was developing indices based on sectors of pan-European stocks, on which it would later launch derivatives.
The president of Belfox's management committee, Jos Schmitt, said the exchange would set up a maximum of three indices in the coming months.

He was speaking at a Management Global Information conference about the future of reglemented derivative markets after the arrival of a European single currency -- the Euro -- and on the future role of Belfox.
"These indices are on sectors. We see only three sectors where European macro-economic elements are predominent compared to national ones," Schmitt said, declining to identify them.

Belfox -- one of Europe's smaller futures and options exchanges -- was talking to organisations about publishing the indices and, once they were established, derivatives, initially futures and options, would be launched on them.
"We can't put a time scale on (the process)," he added. Belfox was also looking for U.S. exchanges interested in its planned pan-European derivatives.
Schmitt said that the prospect of a single currency was part of a wider European convergence, and that national equity indices would gradually fade away.
"They will lose economic meaning," he added.
Belfox also had other strategies for the years ahead.

"We will continue to develop a market in stock options on national shares (where) we still have a lot of potential -- and we will develop a prominent campaign (promoting) national equity derivatives to Belgian and foreign investors," he said.
Belfox would compete by offering new services too.
It would investigate the opportunities of being a "trading gateway," which Schmitt saw as "being a routing mechanism for intermediaries...an access point to different exchanges."
Belfox would also look at the possibilities of being a "clearing gateway" -- a sort of general clearing house, and it was considering providing clearing services for over the counter (OTC) business.
